newsitem.title: UK: LME copper jumpy, ends with pared losses.
newsitem.headline: LME copper jumpy, ends with pared losses.

text.p: Copper business remained volatile during Thursday afternoon LME trading, with the market whipping under $2,150 at one stage only to unlock some buying and end with pared loosses.

Traders said the dip under $2,150 represented a good buying opportunity, while would-be fresh sellers were deterred by the backwardation, which although narrower again today, has the potential to flare up any time.
Other metals were less affected by copper's weakness, and finished mixed, above the lows.
"A lot of the New Year optimism has worn off...but copper still has a sting in its tail," one said.

Copper spreads again eased further forward, while the tight immediate dates remained fully firm. This caused the overall cash/threes backwardation to ease to $200/210 from $250. Meanwhile, cash/one day was at $23 and "tom/next" (belated trading against the previous day's prompt) earlier traded at the LME's $25 limit.

Warehouse stocks are seen rising by between 10,000 and 15,000 tonnes on Friday, although traders are discounting this increase which is due to the high spot premium. Last three months business was at $2,160, down $23, but above the year's low of $2,142.

The aluminium market threatened to break lower at one stage today, but was ably defended, as expected, between $1,600 and $1,610. By the conclusion of the kerb prices were back at $1,614, little changed from the overnight $1,613.
Nickel prices were resilient this afternoon, with the general level of physical interest seen as reasonable, while consumer expectations of further price falls may be unfounded, traders said.
Despite copper's weakness in the last two days, nickel has been well supported when prices have threatened to break down towards $7,100. Last kerb trade was at $7,295, up $115 from yesterday.
Zinc was aided by the U.S Mint tender, where the 2,964 tonnes of SHG metal was bought at an average price that was in excess of 5.50 cents/lb over LME cash.

Traders said the Mint offers and eventual award reflected solid physical interest. There was also support on the early dip towards the $1,120 level, and prices concluded the kerb at $1,135, up $9 from the previous close.

Lead staged a mini-rally from yesterday's 15-month lows, and managed to claw above the $670 level. Last trade was at $674, up $4. Tin similarly mounted a modest recovery, helped by late covering, and closed the kerb at $5,820, against a previous $5,800.
Alloy edged up in slow trading, and finished $15 higher at $1,505 a tonne.
